# `Q-18-4` — Engine Image Output Could Not Be Used

> An execution engine returned an image for a code cell, but Quarto
> could not decode it or write it to disk; the render continues without
> the figure.

## What this means

When a code cell draws a plot, the engine hands Quarto the image data.
Quarto decodes it and saves it as a figure file next to your document
(in the `<document>_files/figure-html/` folder), then points the page at
that file.

This warning means that step failed for one image. The page is still
produced, but that figure is missing: Quarto shows a placeholder
(`[Image output]`), or the output's plain-text form when the cell
produced one. The message names the cell and the reason.

## Why this happens

- The kernel sent image data in a form Quarto could not decode. The
  message says `invalid base64`. This is a bug in how Quarto reads that
  kernel's output, not a problem in your code.
- Quarto could not create the figure folder or write the file, for
  example because of file permissions or a full disk. The message names
  the path and the operating system's reason.

## How to fix

1. If the message names a path, check that the folder next to your
   document is writable and that the disk has room, then re-run the
   render.
2. If the message says `invalid base64`, check that the plot displays
   correctly in the kernel itself. If it does, report it at
   <https://github.com/quarto-dev/q2/issues> with the full warning text
   and the kernel you used.

Use `--strict` to make this warning stop the render instead of
producing a page with a missing figure:

```bash
q2 render --strict
```
